_comment: Per-engine LLM prices in USD per 1M tokens. Manually maintained. Update when providers change pricing. Missing engines log a warning at record time and store cost as 0 (under-counts; not fatal). cached_input_per_1m_usd is read by _cost_for in app/services/llm_call_logger.py — cached portion of input tokens is billed at the cached rate, the rest at input_per_1m_usd. When cached_input_per_1m_usd is absent, full input rate applies to cached tokens too (conservative fallback for engines whose cached rate we don't have).
_source: provider pricing pages; gpt-5 family cached rates on OpenAI's uniform 10%-of-input basis (matches the published 5.4-family entries). gpt-5.6-luna at the 2026-07-30 price cut ($0.20/$1.20).
_opencode_comment: OpenCode Zen (Go plan) is a flat-rate subscription: tokens are drawn against a weekly quota, not billed per token, so the marginal USD cost of a call really is 0. These entries exist to record that deliberately rather than leaving the engines unpriced — an absent entry ALSO records $0 but emits a 'no price entry' warning per engine, which is indistinguishable from a genuine pricing gap. Track OpenCode consumption via token counts and the quota window, not cost_usd. If you switch to pay-as-you-go balance billing (opencode.ai/workspace → available balance), replace these zeros with the per-model rates from the Zen pricing page.
